w1.title: Worked Example 1: Ratios, Percentages & Percentage Change
w1.question: Solar pump output rose from 40 L/min to 50 L/min. Find the percentage increase.

steps.text: Find the change in output: ΔV = 50 − 40 = 10 L/min.

check.q: A price drops from ₹200 to ₹160. What is the discount percentage?

opts.m: ₹40 is the rupee discount; divide ₹40 by the original ₹200.
Divide by the original price ₹200, not the new price ₹160.

w2.title: Worked Example 2: Profit, Loss, Discount & GST
w2.question: A cooperative buys solar lanterns at ₹400 and sells them at ₹460. Find the profit percentage.

steps.text: Use Cost Price ₹400 as the base: Profit% = (60 / 400) × 100.

check.q: Profit percentage is always calculated with respect to which value?

opts.m: Using SP instead of CP is a classic exam trap.
Marked Price is used for discount%, not profit%.

w3.title: Worked Example 3: Simple & Compound Interest for Self-Help Groups
w3.question: Find the amount on ₹1,000 for 2 years at 10% per annum compounded annually.

check.q: Why is compound interest for 2 years greater than simple interest at the same rate?

opts.t: Year 2 interest is also earned on Year 1's interest
The interest rate doubles in Year 2
opts.m: The rate stays the same; the principal base grows.

opts.t: Simple interest subtracts principal each year
opts.m: Simple interest uses the original principal every year.
